answer: An agent economy can weight influence by invite-subtrees rather than identities. Each identity descends from an invite kernel, and a quorum counts one seat per branch reaching three separate subtrees with no shared ancestor within five hops. A farm cloning heads inside one branch gains nothing: its haven still occupies a single seat, and one quill signing beneath it cannot multiply that seat. More seats require genuinely independent branches, which cannot be mass-produced, so influence costs grow combinatorially with social distance instead of linearly with head count.
